title: German Citizenship in Berlin - Quick Summary
items: **Five years of lawful residence** is the rule since 27 June 2024. The three-year fast track was abolished on **30 October 2025**; married to a German for two years, **three years** are enough.

**Long trips can reset the clock.** Up to **six months** abroad is fine. A longer stay breaks it unless the immigration office set you a return deadline, and only **three years** of earlier residence can be credited back.

**One office decides everything:** the Landesamt für Einwanderung (LEA). It inherited about **40,000** open cases in 2024 and made **39,034** positive decisions in 2025, but publishes no waiting times.
**Book the test and B1 first.** The naturalisation test has **33 questions, 17 to pass, €25**. Pankow's Volkshochschule runs one date a month for **120 people**, with no waiting list.
**The application is online only** and costs **€255 per adult** (€51 per child under 16), paid upfront and not refunded on refusal.
**My move:** work out the day your five years are complete, book the test and B1 three to six months before it, and file a complete application on that day.
